note: Updated for two breaking items since the earlier 08-24 file. (1) Josh Jacobs was placed on the NFL Commissioner's Exempt List (announced Sun Aug 23) over five May domestic-abuse charges - out indefinitely, six-game ban the probable baseline. His handcuff MarShawn Lloyd is now the #1 Sleeper add (~284k) and a real ~6-week bell-cow. Stipe owns Jacobs and is now acutely RB-needy with full FAAB - he'll drive a frenzy. (2) Ashton Jeanty (my RB) has a confirmed ankle sprain (low, not major, Week 1 uncertain) - fresh post-draft news, but cushioned: I roster his handcuff Mike Washington plus deep RB (Taylor, Irving, Tuten), so I can field 2 RB + 2 FLEX without him. No add needed for either event - I'm RB-deep enough to pass the Lloyd frenzy and preserve FAAB. Other own-roster watch items unchanged: Egbuka (toe) and LaPorta (hip), both Week-1 uncertain; Ferguson covers LaPorta at TE.

targets.why: Jacobs landed on the Commissioner's Exempt List Sunday (Aug 23) and can't practice or play while on it, with a six-game suspension the probable baseline. That hands Lloyd, his direct handcuff, a bell-cow role in a strong Green Bay offense for roughly six weeks. Now the #1 add on Sleeper (~284k). (Fox Sports / NBC Sports, Aug 2026)
targets.asset: Startable bell-cow RB, 2-FLEX-relevant, for ~6 weeks while Jacobs is out; reverts to a plain Jacobs handcuff after.
targets.my_team_impact: Real weekly points, but I'm already RB-deep: Jonathan Taylor, Ashton Jeanty (ankle, likely fine), Bucky Irving, Bhayshul Tuten, plus Mike Washington. Even with Jeanty's Week-1 risk I can fill 2 RB + 2 FLEX without Lloyd. He would only bump a boom/bust WR dart (Johnston), not a starter.
targets.worth: FAAB 15-20 ceiling to me: a temporary FLEX upgrade over a bench dart, decayed for the ~6-week window and my existing RB depth.
targets.confidence_why: The role is real and locked for ~6 weeks, but I'm RB-deep and the clearing price will be a frenzy - the overpay-for-me is the high-confidence part, not a knock on the player.
targets.competition: Stipe owns Jacobs and just lost him, acutely RB-needy with a full 100 FAAB; expect a frenzy bid (the model's injury-replacement floor is 60+). StoneBone69/DiaperDutyDaddy likely pile on.
targets.bid: Pass. Clearing a desperate Stipe means 60+, off-budget for a 6-week rental I don't need. Let Stipe pay up.
targets.drop: Quentin Johnston if pursuing, but the call is to pass.

targets.why: The Colts have talked openly about managing Jonathan Taylor after his league-high 323 carries; Giddens is listed RB2 on the first unofficial depth chart, with rookie Seth McGowan generating the camp buzz and leading Sleeper adds. Whoever wins the job directly handcuffs a workhorse who would hand his backup a weekly-starter role if he missed time. (IND depth chart, Aug 2026)
targets.asset: Contingent RB1 workload if Taylor misses time; otherwise minimal touches behind a workhorse.
targets.my_team_impact: I roster Jonathan Taylor (RB1) with no handcuff, my only real insurance gap, and with Jeanty now dinged the value of clean RB insurance is a touch higher. In a 5-bench league JT's backup is a league-swinger if he misses time. An add would cost a deep WR dart, not a starter.
targets.worth: FAAB 3-5 ceiling as cheap workhorse insurance, decayed only lightly with a full season ahead.
targets.confidence_why: IND RB2 is an unsettled Giddens-vs-McGowan split; the handcuff is not locked to one player, so buying the wrong half is dead weight.
targets.competition: Seth McGowan (rookie, leading Sleeper adds); both unrostered in-league. No rival owns Taylor, so nobody is racing me.
targets.bid: 0 now, WATCH. Claim the winner for FAAB 2-3 once the final preseason game clarifies the RB2 job; no bidding pressure.
targets.drop: Quentin Johnston or Ja'Kobi Lane, my deepest WR darts.

targets.bid: Pass. My own WR darts (Odunze, Johnston, Lane) are better-situated.
